text:
william: hey all first day, excited to be here. VPN connected (our-agent) but i can't reach the bastion at 10.40.1.2 to ssh. browser to intranet times out. client UI says split-tunnel. anyone know the quick checks?

tara: welcome! two quick checks: which OS, and can you paste `netstat -rn` (mac/linux) or `route print` (win)? also which interface shows the vpn (utun/ppp/etc)?

william: macbook pro intel, macOS Monterey. paste below, redacted my home gateway: 
```
Routing tables:
default            192.168.50.1        UGScg      en0
10.40.0.0/16       192.168.50.1        UGSc       en0   <-- this looks wrong
172.27.10.0/24     172.27.10.1         UGSc       utun2
```

william: so 10.40/16 is going out locally. i tried `ssh 10.40.1.2` and it times out.

ton: that explains it. the VPN didn't push the internal route or mac picked the LAN route because it existed already. quick workaround: `sudo route -n add -net 10.40.0.0/16 172.27.10.1` then `ssh -v william@10.40.1.2`. if the ssh hangs with "No route to host" after adding route, try `sudo dscacheutil -flushcache` for DNS weirdness.

william: added route and ssh connects! thanks. quick q: will that stay after reboot?

tara: it won't by default. options: (1) we can push a policy to your fleet image, (2) add a LaunchAgent plist to reapply at login, or (3) if you have admin and use homebrew you can drop a small shell script in /etc/rc.local. we usually send a plist for new-hires. want me to DM it?

william: pls DM the plist, ty. also curious why this happens only at home sometimes.

ton: common cause: consumer routers that use 10.x/16 spaces or some ISP CGNAT overlaps. split-tunnel clients avoid VPNing all traffic and only push internal subnets; if your LAN advertises the same prefix the OS will prefer the local route. macOS also has interface metric quirks where en0 gets precedence. tethering to a phone hotspot and re-connecting VPN often forces the client to push the correct route because the hotspot uses a different subnet.

william: noted. i did have weird captive portal earlier on the network login screen, could that be related?

tara: yes if the router had a captive portal it can block the client from pulling updated config. always complete Okta SSO before first VPN connection.

okta-bot: Reminder: complete your Okta enrollment by opening the SSO link in your default browser before establishing the VPN session.

william: infra-bot message popped up after adding route, what's that about?

infra-bot: Created INFRA-5012: "split-tunnel route not applied for 10.40/16 on macOS when LAN overlaps" assigned to @jon. Please attach `~/Library/Logs/redwood-agent/agent.log` and `netstat -rn` output.

jon: will follow up. quick heads up: for Windows folks the equivalent is `netsh interface ip add route 10.40.0.0/16 "Your VPN Interface" <vpn-gw-ip> metric=1`. For mac persistent plist i sent DM with this minimal plist snippet and a small wrapper script that calls `route add` on login.

william: got the plist DM and applied it. rebooted and route is back, ssh still works. thanks team!

tara: adding a short note to new-hire checklist: if you see internal IPs routed to your home gateway, add manual route or use phone hotspot for onboarding. saved a lot of triage time. :white_check_mark:

william: one last thing  internal docker registry pull failed earlier, fixed by route. should i include that in my onboarding notes?

ton: yes, please add a line about registry, bastion, and persistent route snippet. i'll link INFRA-5012 so infra can track if it's a class issue.

william: thanks everyone, saved my first-day pairing session :partyparrot:
